root.label: AFGE report on CDC workforce losses through May 2026

events.label: AFGE report on CDC workforce losses through May 2026

slots.name: workforce reduction
slots.sentence: Between March 2025 and May 2026, the CDC's overall workforce has decreased by 30%, stretching across divisions, offices and job fields, according to a new report from the American Federation of Government Employees, a union representing CDC workers.

slots.name: separations
slots.sentence: Over the course of 14 months, an estimated 3,539 "separations" took place within the agency, accounting for layoffs, retirements and those who quit.

slots.name: active employees
slots.sentence: When adding in those who have been placed on administrative leave and are not working, but have not yet been fully let go, there is a total 30% reduction in the workforce, leaving 8,895 active employees.

slots.name: voluntary retirements
slots.sentence: A total of 857 employees took voluntary retirement during that period, while another 837 employees quit.

slots.name: employees quitting
slots.sentence: A total of 857 employees took voluntary retirement during that period, while another 837 employees quit.

slots.name: terminated employees
slots.sentence: Another 642 employees were terminated or their appointments expired, the union said.

slots.name: RIF-affected employees
slots.sentence: A combined 843 employees were considered "RIF-affected," or those who were impacted by "reduction in force" actions.

slots.name: early retirements
slots.sentence: On top of that, 216 employees opted for an early retirement to leave the CDC.

slots.name: center workforce losses
slots.sentence: Office of Human Resources: 320 employees, 98% of workforcee

slots.name: attrition multiple
slots.sentence: "This is not normal," the AFGE Local 2883 said. "CDC lost staff at more than 1.5 (time) the federal rate over the same period."

slots.name: NIOSH workforce loss
slots.sentence: National Institute for Occupational Safety and Health: 312 employees, 30% of workforce

slots.name: Chronic Disease workforce loss
slots.sentence: National Center for Chronic Disease Prevention and Health Promotion: 303 employees, 48% of workforce

slots.name: Emerging Infectious Diseases workforce loss
slots.sentence: National Center for Emerging and Zoonotic Infectious Diseases: 281 employees, 17% of workforce

slots.name: CDC founding date
slots.sentence: Then known as the Communicable Disease Center, the now-CDC was founded in 1946 to help military members at Southern bases stay safe from malaria, later growing to include other communicable diseases and health-related issues like smoking and bioterror.
